alternatives.argument: The local definition is fully explicit about the finite-support algebraic tensor sum, its product and involution, each continuous W_n, the degree-zero normalization, and positivity as a hypothesis. The exact Schwartz and tempered-distribution suppliers are in deps; no reconstruction theorem is inferred from this source.

The local definition specifies H, a dense common domain D, the first-variable-linear pairing, linear maps Phi(f):D->D, and continuity of every scalar matrix coefficient. It is a definition and makes no point-field or self-adjointness claim.

The local definition states the Lorentz matrix, signature, semidirect-product law, affine spacetime action, and test pullback formula. The following local lemma proves its Schwartz-space well-definedness and continuity.

The local definition fixes exp(-i p dot z), proves its relation to the published 2pi Euclidean Fourier automorphism by a Lorentz-sign reflection and dilation, defines transposition on S-prime, and explicitly defines forward-cone support on compact tests.

For fixed Lambda,a, the affine chain rule and x=Lambda y+a bound every pullback seminorm by finitely many Schwartz seminorms. Near identity, set y_t=(I+t(Lambda^-1-I))x-t Lambda^-1 a; for Lambda near I the inverse matrices are uniformly bounded, so 1+|x|<=C(1+|y_t|). The fundamental theorem of calculus writes each derivative difference as the integral of its next derivatives times (Lambda^-1-I)x-Lambda^-1a. After the polynomial weight, this is bounded by epsilon_g times finitely many higher Schwartz seminorms. Chain-rule coefficients also converge to their identity values. Hence T_g f->f in every seminorm; fixed-map continuity and the group law give continuity at every group element. The universal property then gives the algebraic star action.

The complete alternative proof is supplied in the item. Explicitly: the separated-variable product seminorm identity makes W_n evaluations continuous in each test factor; AC_omega and the positive normalized omega give the quotient GNS Hilbert space and common domain. Matrix coefficients of Phi(f)=pi(X(f)) are finite sums of those continuous W_n evaluations, and GNS supplies closability, the adjoint restriction, and exact vacuum moments. Continuity of each Poincare pullback and of J_n makes omega(b* alpha_g(a)) continuous; state invariance then invokes the actual state-symmetry lemma. If all moment pairings with r vanish, pi(r) has zero pairing with a dense domain and is zero. For translations, Cauchy-Schwarz plus invariance bounds D_b,a; continuity makes it regular tempered. The GNS coefficient equals D_b,a, so any assumed transposed Fourier support transfers exactly. All covariance, locality, equation, and spectrum statements retain their displayed extra hypotheses; no joint generators or unspecified positive state are claimed.
